subject: mmc: dw_mmc-pltfm: socfpga: restore maximum data timeout (#105)
author: Kasper Olesen
provenance_doc_ref: Not a provenance-doc row: this is new fork work, not a 5.15 carry. The vanilla behaviour it restores IS 5.15's, but via a hook (drv_data->set_data_timeout) that 5.15's dw_mmc did not have and did not need -- pre-v5.17 __dw_mci_start_request() wrote the maximum TMOUT unconditionally for everyone.

impact.effect_if_absent: On a card slow enough to miss the ~110 ms per-request budget that 6.18/7.2 derive from mmc_set_data_timeout()'s 100 ms, every SD READ request that overruns is retried, then the card is hardware-reset and the request re-read one sector at a time (CMD17 + CMD13 each). Throughput collapses -- the PR measures 22 MB/s -> 0.9 MB/s with the budget artificially shortened to 30 ms. Nothing prints -110, dw_mmc does not touch its debugfs err_stats on this path, and the only dmesg trace is a repeated 'Bus speed (slot 0) = 50000000Hz (slot req 400000Hz ...)' from card re-init. A user sees stutter and long loads, not an error. NOT REPRODUCED at the stock 100 ms setting on any card either side has: the author estimates a card would have to be slower than ~9 MB/s on 1 MB requests, or show ~100 ms internal latency spikes, to trigger it as shipped, and the fork's issue #103 (PSX CHD stutter / slow N64 loads) is only a SUSPECTED instance, unconfirmed on the reporter's card.
affected_hardware: DE10-Nano SD/MMC (Cyclone V DesignWare dw_mmc, altr,socfpga-dw-mshc, 50 MHz controller clock)

userspace_coupling.main_mister_ref: None. The change is entirely inside the block layer's view of the controller; no evdev code, no sysfs name, no ioctl. Main_MiSTer sees only faster or slower reads.

forward_port.effort: none -- applied as authored in BOTH kernels. Measured at patch -p1 -F0 with the full series in order: 6.18.52 offset 0 ('patching file drivers/mmc/host/dw_mmc-pltfm.c', no offset line), 7.2.6 'Hunk #1 succeeded at 86 (offset -10 lines)'. Zero fuzz, zero rejects in both. board/mister/de10nano/linux-patches-beta/ carries a symlink rather than a re-anchored copy because the anchor text is byte-identical across 6.18 and 7.2 -- 7.x rewrote dw_mci_socfpga_priv_init()'s clock-phase parsing ABOVE it and left socfpga_drv_data alone.

license_provenance: GPL-2.0-or-later (the file's own SPDX tag). Author Kasper Olesen <kaspersolesen@gmail.com>, GitHub @kblood (`gh api users/kblood` -> name 'Kasper Olesen'), who opened PR #105 himself, so PR author and commit author are the same person. notes:
NOT a backport and not a revert. The reflex on reading 'restore' is to hunt for the mainline commit that broke it and check whether a stable release has already fixed it. The breaking commit is real -- 6a8c2018e872 ('mmc: dw_mmc: Allow lower TMOUT value than maximum', v5.17) -- but it was a deliberate behaviour change, not a regression anyone upstream has repaired, and there is no fix to backport. What exists instead is a per-platform escape hatch the same generation of work added: drv_data->set_data_timeout (linux-6.18.52 drivers/mmc/host/dw_mmc.h:597,617; 7.2.6 :517,:537), consulted first thing in dw_mci_set_data_timeout() (6.18.52 dw_mmc.c:1285-1293 'if (drv_data && drv_data->set_data_timeout) return drv_data->set_data_timeout(host, timeout_ns);'). Exynos is the only in-tree user in either kernel (dw_mmc-exynos.c:577, :649). So the carry adds a socfpga user of an upstream hook; no core code changes.

MEASURED ABSENT FROM BOTH PINS, not inferred from one. `grep -n set_data_timeout drivers/mmc/host/dw_mmc-pltfm.c` returns nothing (exit 1) in linux-6.18.52 AND in linux-7.2.6, both extracted from tarballs checked against this repo's own recorded signed-manifest hashes before use (board/mister/de10nano/patches/linux/linux.hash sha256 2b69564f...; package/linux-rt/linux-rt.hash sha256 039aef84...). That matters because 'in mainline' is not the question -- 'in the kernel WE BUILD' is, the lesson 6332499e7's record records.

WHY THE SOFTWARE TIMER FOLLOWS THE REGISTER, which is the part of the mechanism that makes a one-line writel sufficient: dw_mci_set_drto() does not keep its own budget, it reads TMOUT back -- 6.18.52 dw_mmc.c:2003-2025, 'drto_clks = mci_readl(host, TMOUT) >> 8;' then 'drto_ms += 10;'. Programming the maximum in the hook therefore lengthens both the hardware timeout and the software data-read timer, which is exactly the 5.15 shape.

SOURCE IDENTITY MEASURED. With the full series applied in order to pristine 6.18.52 and to pristine 7.2.6, the region from 'static void dw_mci_socfpga_set_data_timeout' to 'static const struct of_device_id dw_mci_pltfm_match' diffs EMPTY against `git show 7a65ca02c:drivers/mmc/host/dw_mmc-pltfm.c` in both trees.

DE25 DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, and this is the first mmc patch where the two boards genuinely diverge. socfpga_drv_data is reached only via `{ .compatible = "altr,socfpga-dw-mshc", .data = &socfpga_drv_data, }` (dw_mmc-pltfm.c:105 / :95); the Agilex 5 SD controller is a Cadence SDHCI part (board/mister/de25nano/linux-patches/0101-mmc-sdhci-cadence-agilex5-40-bit-dma-mask.patch), and board/mister/de25nano/linux.config has no CONFIG_MMC_DW at all -- its MMC block is CONFIG_MMC_SDHCI/_PLTFM/_CADENCE=y at lines 178-180 -- so dw_mmc-pltfm.c is not even compiled there. board/mister/de10nano/linux.config:510 has CONFIG_MMC_DW=y. Contrast 0020-mmc-no-led-on-send-status, which IS on all three series because it changes the mmc CORE. Recorded as a row in board/mister/de25nano/linux-patches/README.md.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, carried forward deliberately rather than rounded off: the failure mode is demonstrated with an artificially shortened (30 ms) budget, not with a card that fails at the stock 100 ms. The cost of carrying is bounded and stated -- a genuinely unresponsive card now takes ~346 ms instead of ~110 ms to fail a read, and writes are unaffected because their 3 s limit already clamped to the maximum. Boot-tested by the author on a DE10-Nano (TMOUT reads back 0xFFFFFFFF, exFAT ~22 MB/s and raw ~23 MB/s unchanged, 19584-byte random reads p50 1.73 ms); NOT exercised on this project's rig, which is the open item for this row.
